notification_proxy(8) System Manager's Manual notification_proxy(8)

NAME

notification_proxy — notification server

SYNOPSIS

notification_proxy

DESCRIPTION

notification_proxy enables a trusted remote Mac to read/write notifications on this Mac. Trust requires that this Mac explicitly pair with the remote Mac. The daemon is started automatically by launchd upon the trusted Mac requesting a connection to this service.

A trusted remote Mac may also read and write the 64-bit state value that the notify server keeps for a notification name. Every relayed notification carries the state of its name with it, so the remote Mac sees the value as of the moment the notification fired. Reading a single name on demand is answered as a reply to the request, and so is served only over RemoteXPC; the lockdown transport has no reply channel. A state written this way lasts only while that remote Mac stays connected, because the notify server discards the state for a name once the last registration for that name is released. No form of state access, including the state carried by a relay, is offered to untrusted remote Macs.

This daemon also allows an untrusted remote Mac to read/write notifications while this Mac is still in setup. Once this Mac exits device setup, trust is required.

This command is not intended to be invoked directly.

SEE ALSO

notify(3).
